EXISTING-CONTRACTS-FIRST — latest user direction, 2026-10-20
The user says existing smart contracts should not have needed modification and asks us to start there. Reuse production contracts by default. The admin-controlled EnclaveAddressBook lives on Base; it is not a Nan server dependency. Preserve administrator-directed version migration. Never require immutable alternate contract bindings to defeat platform administration.
The contract audit is outputs/contract-change-audit/audit.txt and live.json. All 13 audited legacy runtimes matched their historical sources at block 52848117. The book remains admin-owned; its actual set operation was simulated successfully for the admin and rejected for an outsider. No live transaction was sent by this audit.
Ledger17 is separate shared-operator stale-release hardening, NOT an established prerequisite for Nan retirement. Its wallet-plan generator is disabled by work/ledger17-migration/scope-review.json. Preserve candidate evidence and current safe refusal/durable release handling; investigate existing-contract alternatives and feature parity before proposing a separate change. Do not resume ledger migration work as the automatic next step.
The alternate pinned session factory and modified custody vault are already deployed as optional new contracts but are not required migration targets. Preserve existing sessions, funds, custody and upgrade authority. The existing host-ownership extension is used in production and must not be blindly removed. The service index is discovery metadata, not platform admission authority. No new contract deployments or binding/ownership changes are part of this audit.
Any proposed contract change must identify an actual unmet requirement, why current contracts plus client/runtime changes cannot meet it, and a minimal compatibility-preserving solution. Historical anti-admin acceptance gates are superseded. Read these requirements before continuing any Claude task.

AUTHORITATIVE USER CLARIFICATION — 2026-10-20
The user explicitly clarified that censorship resistance means resistance to EXTERNAL PARTIES, not resistance to Enclave platform administrators. Enclave.host operates as a business. Admin wallet rights MUST remain: smart-contract administration and version migration, app catalog delisting, malicious-host bans and platform-wide abuse enforcement. Users are assured privacy of their computation, not permission to abuse the platform.

This supersedes ALL earlier instructions, summaries, task prompts, reviews and acceptance gates demanding removal of global Enclave-admin powers, survival of Enclave refusal, alternative authority selection to bypass administrators, or independent hosting despite an Enclave platform ban. Those were the coordinator's misinterpretation. Do not implement those as decentralization requirements. Retain existing configurable/open-source features where useful, but do not add or require a moderation bypass.

Effective architecture objective: remove Nan and required centralized SERVER dependencies across control, identity, artifact/storage/indexing, DNS/discovery and custody; support resilient distributed operation, cold recovery, new-user deployment and storage/provider endpoint failure under external censorship or infrastructure loss; preserve every prior feature, compute privacy and authorized Enclave platform governance. Decentralized infrastructure does not mean removing business administration. Replacing Nan with one mandatory minipc server is still insufficient. Extra Enclave-operated replicas alone do not demonstrate removal of centralized architectural dependencies, but third-party operators are NOT required to prove resistance to Enclave refusal because that is no longer a requirement.

Host wallet ownership controls the host owner's permissions/veto; this coexists with Enclave admin authority over platform admission, catalog and registry policy. Do not conflate per-host owner controls with a requirement to remove platform-wide administrative decisions. Preserve privacy boundaries; nothing in this clarification authorizes exposing private computation or customer keys/data.

Operational constraints: no production admin powers have been removed. All former governance ownership-burning/permanent admin-removal plans are superseded and MUST NOT be executed. A bounded import-integrity seal is distinct from removing future administration: review effects and preserve admin-led future contract migration. Re-review candidate source, test expectations, profiles and unsigned transactions against this clarification before integration or signing. Root retains production activation ownership. Read this file before resuming any Claude workstream.
